cross_metric_analysis: FUNNEL RETENTION: Shrinking the candidate pool from 100 to 20 retains 17.2% of the recall (Recall drops from 1.60% to 0.27%).
SURFACING SPEED LIFT: The Ranker improved MRR@20 by 454.9% (from 0.01 to 0.03). The Cross-Encoder successfully pushes the first relevant item much closer to rank 1.
RANKER LIFT: The Ranker improved NDCG@20 by 406.7% over pure retrieval. The Cross-Encoder is successfully refining the candidate slates.
SUCCESSFUL FILTERING: The Ranker aggressively filtered out 100.0% of the Retriever's items, resulting in a positive NDCG lift of 406.7%. It successfully separated the signal from the ANN's noise.
RANKER COVERAGE COLLAPSE: To achieve its ranking, the Ranker sacrificed 26.5% of the Retriever's catalog coverage. It is behaving much more conservatively than the ANN.

ITEM COLD-START RESILIENCE (RETRIEVER): When 501 test movies are replaced with unmemorized OOV=0 phantom items, Recall@100 retains 545.2% of warm performance (8.71% vs 1.60%). The Candidate Tower's content features (genres/metadata) generalize strongly into the embedding space.

ITEM COLD-START RANKER LIFT: Even with OOV=0 phantom movies in the candidate pool, the Ranker improves NDCG@20 by 76.4% (and MRR@20 by 85.9%) over pure retrieval. The GATv2 graph attention effectively scores cold-start item embeddings against user history.

HEAD ITEM ID DEPENDENCY: Under cold-start movie simulation, Tier 0 (head) NDCG@20 drops by -136.6% (1.21% -> 2.86%), compared to a -344.3% change for Tier 2 (long-tail) items. Popular items rely heavily on memorized collaborative ID weights rather than metadata.
STRONG DEMOGRAPHIC COLD-START (USER RETRIEVER): With user_id=0 (OOV), demographic features alone (age, gender, occupation) retain 157.3% of warm Recall@100 (2.51% vs 1.60%, 1.0x random baseline).
ZERO-HISTORY GRAPH RANKER LIFT: Even when cold-start users have an empty watch history in the GATv2 subgraph, the Ranker improves NDCG@20 by 304.2% (and MRR@20 by 543.2%) over pure retrieval.

POWER USER HISTORY ABLATION: Stripping Power Users (Tier 0) of their interaction history and user ID reduces Ranker Recall@20 from 1.53% to 0.86% (confirming that learned history + ID provides a +77.5% relative lift over raw demographics).

COLD-START BOTTLENECK (USER SIDE): End-to-end Ranker NDCG@20 retention is significantly lower for Cold-Start Users (146.6% of warm) than Cold-Start Movies (281.8% of warm). Onboarding new users (e.g., via interactive preference elicitation or richer user features) is a higher-leverage priority than item metadata.
